market_news.paragraph: Global equities were broadly weaker in the latest completed round of trading, with 8 of the 24 benchmarks tracked on this page closing higher. In the United States, the S&P 500 fell 0.71 per cent to 7,631.47, the Dow Jones fell 0.79 per cent to 52,767, the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.03 per cent to 26,100 and the Russell 2000 fell 1.23 per cent to 2,920.13. In Europe, the FTSE 100 was little changed at 10,789, the DAX fell 1.51 per cent to 25,970 and the CAC 40 fell 0.22 per cent to 8,301.85. Across Asia, the Nikkei 225 rose 0.13 per cent to 66,215, the Hang Seng fell 0.92 per cent to 25,330, the KOSPI fell 1.11 per cent to 6,835.80, the Shanghai Composite rose 0.59 per cent to 3,979.89, the BSE Sensex was little changed at 76,944 and the Straits Times rose 0.46 per cent to 5,710.37. Elsewhere, the Ibovespa rose 1.30 per cent to 179,722. Locally, the S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.32 per cent to 9,066.70 and the All Ordinaries rose 0.19 per cent to 9,260.90. In digital assets, bitcoin changed hands at $77,204, down 2.20 per cent over the past 24 hours. In currencies, the US dollar bought 1.4003 Australian dollars, up 0.29 per cent against the prior business day's fix. Index levels, exchange rates and commodity prices on this page are captured live at build time from the sources linked in each section; no forward-looking view is offered here.
